speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish tint to your skin and eyes. To understand the cause of this jaundice, have you noticed any severe abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of cocaine use and high-risk sexual behavior, could you describe any recent symptoms like dark urine, clay-colored stools, nausea, or confusion? Also, have you had any new sexual partners or been exposed to hepatitis or HIV in the last few months?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis (likely Hepatitis B or C given the high-risk sexual history and cocaine use), presenting with jaundice and agitation.
